# P3.8 The reader keeps forwarding the child's stdout after `ready`

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Parent | P3 |
| Role | IMPLEMENTATION |
| Level | L3 |
| Contracts | C-BRIDGE@1, C-ISO@1 |
| Depends | P3.3 |
| Findings | R04, R05 (P3.3's — this card changes the code those two findings produced) |
| Confidence | reproduced in source at this card's base: `src-tauri/src/main.rs:298` breaks the read loop the moment `ready` has been handled, so the forwarding arms at `:318-325` are unreachable after that point — and the `ChildGone` arm at `:326-336` has no `settled` test, while the `!settled` tail at `:340` shows the author knew the pattern |

## Objective

**One behaviour:** after the `ready` line has been handled, `drive` keeps
forwarding the bundled server's unrecognised stdout lines to stderr, until the
child exits or the window closes — instead of leaving the loop at that instant —
**and every line a run can produce after the `ready` has settled is logged and
ignored: a `ChildGone`, a `fatal`, an `Other`, a `Rejection` — with the `ready`
line itself still exactly one.** The second clause is not a second behaviour: it is what the first one
costs. Keeping the loop alive makes the `ChildGone` arm reachable at every
ordinary server exit, and that arm (`main.rs:326-336`) calls `show_error` with no
`settled` test, so a normal post-`ready` exit would paint
`Apunta — exited_before_ready` over a working app unless the arm is guarded.

Nothing else changes. The single navigation stays single, the early-exit path
stays an early exit, the error screen stays an error screen, and the
`settled` bookkeeping keeps deciding exactly what it decides today.

**And the negative control has to be able to say no.** The second clause above is
a claim about what the shell does *not* paint, so the row that witnesses it (V4)
must be able to fail on its own: it identifies the windows it talks about —
owner pid plus exact title, on a pinned display — and every witness it keeps is a
positive statement about a window it has named or a pid it has signalled. A
witness that asserts only the absence of something the reader cannot name is
vacuously true, and a vacuously true witness in a negative control is worse than
no control: it is a green light. Where a witness cannot be made positive the row
is `NOT RUN` with that cause, never a pass.

### Why this card exists, and why the defect is real

`docs/v2/state/AMENDMENTS.md` row **AM-138** records the owner's decision and the
diagnosis; row **AM-140** is the authorisation for this card and it names both
contracts and the mandatory negative-control row. The defect, verified against the
file at this card's base:

- The reader thread (`main.rs:240-252`) drains the child's **stdout** line by
  line and sends every line on as `Event::Bridge(parsed, line)`. That part is
  correct and is not this card's business.
- `drive` (`main.rs:284`) iterates that channel. Its two forwarding arms —
  `Event::Bridge(Ok(Message::Other { kind }), _)` at `:318-320` and
  `Event::Bridge(Err(rejection), line)` at `:321-325` — both `eprintln!` to
  stderr and both fall through to the next line. **These arms are the delivery
  chain, and they work** (P3.4's AM-131 recorded it working in attempt 2).
- The `ready` arm at `:291-306` calls `show_main`, closes the splash, sets
  `settled = true`, and then **exits the loop**:

  > ```rust
  >                 if show_main(&handle, port) {
  >                     close_window(&handle, "splash");
  >                     settled = true;
  >                     break;
  >                 }
  > ```
  > — `src-tauri/src/main.rs:295-299`

  Every line the child writes from that moment on is read off the pipe by the
  reader thread, pushed onto a channel whose only receiver has left, and
  dropped. `drive` then parks in the tail loop at `:354-360`, which does
  `Ok(_) => continue` — it **discards** what arrives.

So the chain is intact at both ends and severed in the middle. P3.4's
observation hook (`docs/v2/cards/P3.4.md:542`, V2's channel description) can
only publish once the page exists, and the page only exists after `ready`, so
its in-page assertions can never be observed: **five `NOT RUN` assertions, and
P3.4 BLOCKED at 3/3.**

And the fix has a price, which the base file already shows: the same loop's
`ChildGone` arm is unconditional, so removing the `break` hands it every ordinary
exit. The remedy is two parts of one control-flow change, both inside `fn drive`
— see May edit and Fixed decision 1.

## May edit

**`src-tauri/src/main.rs`, and inside it only `fn drive` (`:284-361`) — exactly
two named parts and nothing else: (i) the `ready` arm's control flow, i.e. the
success-path `break` at `:298`; and (ii) the `ChildGone` arm's `settled` test,
i.e. the `show_error` / `close_window` / `break` block at `:329-335` must not
run once `settled` is already true.**

That is the whole of it. One file, one function, two parts of one control-flow
decision.

**No third part is authorised, and no other file is.** A third part — a new arm,
a second `settled` flag, a moved or recomputed `settled`, a rewritten
`show_error`, a change to the `fatal` arm, to the `!settled` tail or to the
terminal drain — is **Stop condition 3**, and a second file is Stop condition 2.
Part (ii) is authorised because it is *inside the same file and the same
function* as part (i), and because the owner recorded the defect's second half in
AM-140 ("not painted when it dies after"); the coordinator confirmed it in source
at `main.rs:329-335`, where the `ChildGone` arm calls `show_error` with no
`settled` test while the `if !settled` guard a few lines later shows the pattern
the file already uses.

## Fixed decisions

1. **The change is two named parts of one control-flow decision in `fn drive`,
   and nothing that could reasonably be called a third.**
   **(i) Remove the success-path `break` at `:298`.** After `show_main`
   succeeds the `ready` arm falls through to the next event like every other
   arm. The `settled = true` assignment **stays**, because `settled` is what
   tells the `:340-348` tail that the launch succeeded and must not paint an
   error screen over a working app — and it is now also the input to part (ii).
   **(ii) Make the `ChildGone` arm a no-op once `settled` is already true** —
   log it, and do **not** `show_error`, do **not** `close_window`, and either
   `continue` or leave the loop without painting.
   *Why (ii) is not optional, and why it is not scope creep:* with (i) alone,
   the next event the loop receives is the `ChildGone` the reader thread sends
   the moment `child.wait()` returns (`main.rs:250-251`) — which is what it
   sends whenever the child exits, including the ordinary case of a server that
   was working and then stopped. That arm (`main.rs:326-336`) is unconditional
   today, so (i) alone paints `Apunta — exited_before_ready` over a healthy app
   on a normal shutdown. Fixed decision 6, V4(e), V4(f) and AM-140's "not
   painted when it dies after" all forbid that, and the coordinator confirmed the
   missing `settled` test in source. Both parts live in the **same file and the
   same function**, which is where AM-140's "exactly the forwarding loop in
   `src-tauri/src/main.rs`" is satisfied. Anything beyond these two parts is Stop
   condition 3.
2. **The `break` at `:305` — the window-would-not-open path — stays exactly as
   it is.** That arm is C-BRIDGE@1 rule 7's shape: an error screen rather than
   a splash that never resolves, and then the shell is done. Removing it would
   leave the shell forwarding lines from a server nobody is looking at, behind
   an error window, for the rest of its life. Only the **success** `break` goes.
3. **`show_main` is called at most once in the process lifetime, and this is
   asserted, not asserted-in-a-paragraph.** V4(a) counts the shell's own
   `apunta: the main window is open on …` stderr lines (`main.rs:517`, written
   by `show_main` on success) and fails the row unless there is exactly one
   across the whole run; V4 also counts the `ready` line. The count is the
   assertion because a second `show_main` cannot be **silent**, not because it
   cannot be built: a duplicate call **does** compile — the window label is a
   runtime string, and `main.rs:469` is only the `WebviewWindowBuilder::new(`
   call — but the label `main` is already taken at `main.rs:471`, so the second
   `build()` returns `Err`, `show_main` takes its `Err` branch (`main.rs:519`,
   `apunta: the main window could not be opened: …`), returns `false`, and the
   `ready` arm then falls into its `:302` failure path and paints
   `the_window_would_not_open`. That is why V4(a) counts the success line rather
   than trusting compilation, and why V4's `c-ready-line-count` is the predicate
   that catches the case.
   **The count is not independent of the change it judges** (V4's Expected cell
   says so in full): it reads a stream the change itself influences, which is why
   it is labelled **supporting** in V4 and never reported as the control. The
   control is the window-identity half — V4(b), (d1), (d2), (e) and (f) — which is
   read from the windows the launch's own pid owns and which a change cannot make
   pass by printing less or printing more. C-BRIDGE@1 rule 1 makes the single
   navigation load-bearing: a second `show_main` after `ready` is a
   re-navigation, which is Stop condition 1 and a contract break regardless of
   how the row's other assertions read.
4. **`Ready` is never swallowed.** The `eprintln!` at `:292` fires on every
   `ready` line the child writes, whether or not the loop then continues. A
   change that keeps forwarding but drops or defers that line has broken
   P3.4's harness's ability to find the boundary between "before ready" and
   "after ready", and V3 and V4 both assert the `ready` line is present on
   stderr **before** the marker line.
5. **stderr is the only destination.** No new file, no log file, no ring
   buffer, no IPC, no environment variable, no new capability. The forwarding
   is `eprintln!`, which is what `:318-325` already does and what P3.4's
   harness already reads. This defect is fixed by *not stopping*, not by
   *adding a channel*.
6. **The child and the reader thread must stay distinguishable at shutdown, and
   the rule covers every event, not only `ChildGone`.** Four clauses:
   **(a)** a `ChildGone` arriving **before** any `ready` must still paint an
   error screen, because that is C-BRIDGE@1 rule 7's early exit; **(b)** a
   `ChildGone` arriving **after** a settled `ready` must be **logged and
   ignored** — no `show_error`, no `close_window`, nothing painted; **(c)** the
   same holds for **any other line arriving after a settled `ready`** — a
   `fatal`, an `Other`, a `Rejection` — because the `fatal` arm at `:307-317`
   is exactly as unconditional as `ChildGone` (`show_error` at `:313`,
   `close_window` at `:314`, `break` at `:316`) and becomes newly reachable the
   moment `:298` goes. Clause (c) is a statement about reachability, not a third
    part of the change: **the card does not edit the `fatal` arm.** What it
    requires is that the change make such a line harmless in that state or leave
    it unreachable by construction; if a `fatal`, an `Other` or a `Rejection`
    arriving after a settled `ready` would still paint, the shell has lost the
    distinction and that is Stop condition 3. (A second `Ready` is not in this
    clause — it is (c-ii) below.) Today no code path produces a post-`ready`
    `fatal` (`server/src/index.ts` writes `Fatal` only at startup), so V4 asserts clause
    (c) over the events the run can actually produce — the post-`ready`
    `ChildGone` — and says so rather than manufacturing one.
    **(c-ii) A `Ready` arriving after a settled `ready`** is the same case and is
    the only line besides `fatal` that can paint: the `main` label is taken at
    `main.rs:471`, so the second `show_main` returns `false` (`main.rs:519`) and
    the arm would paint `the_window_would_not_open` at `:302`. **C-BRIDGE@1 rule 1
    says the server prints exactly one `ready` line**, so no code path produces
    one, and V4's `c-ready-line-count` asserts exactly one over the whole run.
    **The card does not authorise a guard on the `ready` arm** — part (i) only
    removes the success `break`, and a `settled` test inside the `ready` arm
    would be a third part and Stop condition 3. **A second `ready` is Stop
    condition 1: reported, not repaired.** Do not "make it idempotent".
    V4(e) and V4(f) assert clauses (b) and (c) where they can be observed from
    outside, and **V4's pre-`ready` witnesses assert clause (a) twice over**,
    because there are two pre-`ready` ways for the server to fail and only one of
    them can be reached without winning a race: **(d1)** the row holds its own
    loopback listener on 7860, so the server cannot bind, cannot write `ready`
    and exits through its own `EADDRINUSE` path
    (`server/src/index.ts:202-203`) — the `fatal` arm, no timing involved at all;
    **(d2)** the row signals the server's pid `SIGKILL` on the pid line itself,
    polled every 50 ms rather than once a second, which is the `ChildGone` arm.
    Neither is a new code path and neither touches May edit: (d1) is a socket the
    row opens and closes on its own port, (d2) is the pid-scoped signal the card
    already used. **If (d1) and (d2) disagree — one paints and the other does
    not — that is a finding for the coordinator, not a witness to be re-weighted**,
    because the two arms are different arms and Fixed decision 1 authorises a
    guard on only one of them.
7. **The end-to-end row's publisher is a route that already exists, driven by
   the server's own request logger — no server edit, no new route, no marker in
   the bundle.** The bundled server runs Fastify with `logger: true`
   (`server/src/app.ts:70`), so **every request's URL is written to the child's
   stdout (fd 1)** by the request logger; that is the same channel P3.4's hook
   uses, and P3.4's own card says so. V3 therefore drives `GET /api/health` with
   a run-unique query string, **after** the app window is up, and asserts the
   marker reaches stderr. The route exists, the logger exists, and neither is
   touched. **If the observed line does not name the request at all**, that is a
   finding for the coordinator and Stop condition 2 — the card may **not**
   respond by adding a log line, a route, an env var or a build flag.
8. **Every C-BRIDGE@1 rule still holds, and V1 re-runs the tests that hold
   them.** The thirteen `#[test]` cases in `mod tests` (`main.rs:705` onward) are
   unchanged and are re-run by V1: they carry P3.3's navigation guards
   (`main.rs:486-487`, rule 5), the nonce and protocol checks on the bridge
   parser (rule 1), the unknown-type handling (rule 2), and the code-to-word
   mapping. **V1 runs `cargo test` and it must report the same thirteen passing
   and zero failing — no test is deleted, renamed, `#[ignore]`d, or loosened to
   accommodate the change.** A lifecycle change that needs a weakened guard is a

   `:705` holds exactly thirteen `#[test]` attributes); **if a dispatch finds a
   different number of attributes, the *expectation* is corrected to match the
   file and reported — never the tests.**

the row records the display geometry it was given and reports `NOT RUN` on any other; run **after** V3 and never concurrently with it or with anything else on the machine desktop) | exit 0. **This is the negative control, and it exists because a change to a lifecycle loop can pass a smoke test while breaking the thing the loop exists for.** V3 alone would go green on a loop that re-navigated on every forwarded line, re-opened the window each time it saw something, or swallowed `ready` and only then started forwarding. It asserts the negative space. **How the row observes a window — the defect AM-150 found in the previous V4, and why every witness below is now positive.** No window manager is installed on this host (`openbox`, `fluxbox`, `matchbox-window-manager`, `twm`, `metacity`, `xfwm4`, `icewm`, `jwm`, `i3` and `wmctrl` are all absent) and acquiring one is outside this card (L3 isolation discipline, HS-3), so the row does not run under one. The previous row therefore saw **one unnamed window at X's default 640×480**, could not say which window it was looking at, and its two *absence* witnesses — "no window titled with an early-exit word is present" — were **vacuously true**: they read identically whether or not the guard works, which is a false green shaped exactly like success. So the row now identifies every window before it says anything about one, and every claim below is about a window it has named. `snap` prints `id:owner-pid:title:geometry` for every window on the display — `xdotool search --name ".*"` and then **four** separate calls per window (`getwindowpid`, `getwindowname`, `getwindowgeometry --shell`, `getdisplaygeometry`), the multi-call shape `scripts/v2/tauri-lifecycle.test.mjs:297-313` records, with `--onlyvisible` still omitted for the reason that file gives. `appsnap <pid>` then selects the windows the launch's **own shell** owns, by owner pid from `getwindowpid`, so identification is **owner pid plus an exact title**, never a substring and never "the only window there is": `apunta`, the hidden 20×20 GTK helper whose name differs from the app window's only by case, does not match `:Apunta:`, and P3.3's own attempt-2 run read exactly this shape on this host (`docs/v2/evidence/P3.3/attempt2-V3-launch.md`: `apunta 20x20@20,20 pid=168697` and `Apunta 1760x1200@36,26 pid=168697`, both owned by the shell). **The backend must be forced, and this is the fourth instance of the cannot-fail class — the first that would have produced a false GREEN.** This host is a Wayland-capable session (`GDK_BACKEND=wayland`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` set), and under `xvfb-run` there is **no Wayland compositor at all**, so a GTK app that inherits the session backend opens its windows on a display no X client can read. The app is **healthy** either way — it starts, binds and serves `/api/formats` and `/api/settings` at `200` — and it still reports **zero windows** (`docs/v2/evidence/P3.8/B1-diagnostic.md`, AM-159). **The failure mode is an empty list, not an error**, and an empty list is exactly what the *absence* witnesses below read as success: "no window titled `port_in_use` is present" and "no window titled `Apunta` is present" would both hold with the error window sitting there unreadable. So the row's body sets **`GDK_BACKEND=x11` and `XDG_BACKEND=x11` and unsets `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`** as its first statements, inside the `bash -c` body and before any launch, so the settings are in force for all four launches and cannot be lost between the wrapper and the app. With them applied the identification above works on this host: the main window is titled **exactly `Apunta`**, is **owned by the app's own pid**, and measures **1330x950**, above the 880x600 minimum this row asserts. **Three consequences, each one recorded here so it is not rediscovered the hard way.** **(i) Enumeration must tolerate empty fields**, because `xdotool search --name ".*"` returns windows with **no name and no pid** on this host — the X root (1400x1000) and two 1x1 windows. `snap` tolerates them because its substitutions expand to the empty string, and **`appsnap` excludes them structurally rather than by luck**: `grep -E "^[^:]+:$1:"` requires a non-empty id, then a colon, then the pid, then a colon, and a nameless window cannot produce that shape. This is why `appsnap` selects on the **owner-pid field** and not by substring over the whole `id:pid:title:geometry` line — a substring match admits any window whose **title** embeds `:<pid>:`, and positive identification is the entire basis of this control, so the selection is anchored (`AM-157` D1). **(ii) The splash is titled `Apunta — starting` at 720x720 and is gone within ~2 s** of the main window appearing, and **no witness here races it**: every title test is colon-delimited (`:Apunta:` requires a colon on both sides, `:Apunta .*port_in_use:` requires the code word in the same field), so `Apunta — starting` matches none of them, and the only witness that could have raced it — the byte-identical snapshot comparison — runs long after `/api/health` has answered, by which time the splash is gone. **(iii) No window manager exists** (`_NET_SUPPORTING_WM_CHECK` reports `no such atom on any window`, then `not found.`), so the positive-assertion route is **forced, not chosen**, and this card does not install one. **The row also gates each snapshot on being non-empty** (`test -s` on `win.d1` and `win.d2`, `NOT RUN` naming the cause), so that an empty enumeration is refused outright rather than being carried into an absence witness. And the sandbox is entered with **`sandbox.mjs env`, never `sandbox.mjs run`**: `run` starts a server of its own in the data folder, so the app then refuses with `data_folder_in_use` against a holder that was not there a second earlier — that refusal is the wrapper's, not a card defect. **If the row cannot identify the app's window it stops `NOT RUN` and names which half failed** — no window owned by the shell pid, not exactly one window titled exactly `Apunta`, or an `Apunta` window under 880×600, which is the app's own `MIN_WIDTH`/`MIN_HEIGHT` — because a row that cannot name the window it is asserting about has no witness at all, and that is `NOT RUN` and never a pass. For the same reason the display is pinned to `xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1400x1000x24"`, the size P3.3 proved and this host's `xvfb-run` default of 640×480 is not, and a smaller screen is `NOT RUN` rather than a geometry assertion against a window the display itself clamped. **The witnesses, and how each one can fail.** The control is the window-identity half; the log halves support it and are labelled as supporting, because a change that prints less or more controls its own stderr and **the change judging itself is not a control**. **(a) no re-navigation — supporting.** The row counts the shell's own `apunta: the main window is open on …` lines (`main.rs:517`) and requires **exactly one**, beside exactly one `ready` line; it reads a stream the change itself influences, so it is reported alongside and never instead of the window witnesses, and it is not sufficient on its own. **(b) the window was not re-opened — primary and positive.** The row records the identified app-owned window set **before** the marker request and again after it, and requires all three of: the whole-display snapshots byte-identical, the identified app-owned set byte-identical, and the **identified main window's id still present** (`^<id>:<pid>:` in the app-owned snapshot). It **fails** if a second window owned by the shell appears, if the main window's id, title or geometry changes, or if it disappears — which is how "re-show the main window on every forwarded line" announces itself, now caught by identity rather than by the absence of a title. **(c) `ready` is not swallowed — supporting, with the window identity beside it.** Exactly one `ready` line, its line number lower than the marker's, both read with `grep -n` on the captured stderr (Fixed decision 4), **and** the identified main window still present afterwards; it **fails** if the `ready` line is missing or duplicated or if the marker does not follow it. **(d1) a pre-`ready` failure still paints — primary, and it wins no race at all.** The row starts its **own** loopback listener on `127.0.0.1:7860` (a one-line `python3` socket bind, recorded by pid, signalled by pid, released before the next launch) and then launches the AppImage. The bundled server cannot bind, so it cannot write `ready` — it listens before it writes that line (`server/src/index.ts:145`) — and it exits by its own documented path, `writeFatal(PORT_IN_USE_CODE)` at `server/src/index.ts:202-203` and `exit 1`, so the shell's `fatal` arm (`main.rs:307-317`) is what paints. The row asserts the **positive consequence**: exactly one window owned by this shell whose title carries `port_in_use`, and **no** window owned by it titled `Apunta`; and it reports `NOT RUN` if a `ready` line ever appears in that capture, which would mean no pre-`ready` failure was exercised. It **fails** if the error screen is not painted, or if the app window was painted anyway, and there is no timing in it at all — no window to win, which is why this is the primary half of (d). **(d2) the `ChildGone`-before-`ready` arm specifically — primary, with its race repaired rather than retried.** The previous row polled the capture **once per second** for the pid line while the gap between that line and `ready` is **~580 ms** on this host, so the window in which the pre-`ready` exit could be caught was **smaller than the row's own sampling interval** and the race could not be won at all; that is why V4 was `NOT RUN` twice. The row now polls every **50 ms** and signals with `SIGKILL` on the pid from the pid line, so the child cannot finish starting. The margin runs the safe way under load: that ~580 ms is the server's own startup work, which **lengthens** when the box is busy, while the sampling granularity stays at 50 ms. **The verdict does not rest on that margin either**: the row re-reads the whole capture afterwards and is `NOT RUN` — not a pass, and not a `FAIL` dressed as one — if a `ready` line appears at any point, and it is `NOT RUN` at the moment of signalling if one was already there. Its positive witness is that exactly one window owned by this shell is titled with one of the shell's own early-exit words (`exited_before_ready`, `exited_75_without_a_bridge_line`, `terminated_before_ready` — `early_exit_code`, `main.rs:378-388`) and that no `Apunta` window is present; it **fails** if the pre-`ready` exit paints nothing. **That three-word test is a loop, and it must stay one.** The pattern used to be written as one alternation, `early_exit_code`… — and a GFM table cell forces a `\|` into it, while **BRE reads `\|` as alternation and ERE reads it as a literal**, so the row as it sat in the file could never match and would have reported `d2-no-early-exit-error-window` **against a perfect guard** (`AM-157` D2). That is the **third** instance of one root cause (AM-154's bare `\|` in a BRE was the first, which could never fire), and the root cause is structural, not a forgotten backslash: **a card cannot safely hold a regex that needs alternation.** So the row now calls `earlyexit <file>`, which loops over the three words and matches each on its own, and **the row emits no alternation at all** — each of `exited_before_ready`, `exited_75_without_a_bridge_line` and `terminated_before_ready` is matched by a pattern containing **no pipe**, and a file carrying none of them matches none. **No regex anywhere in this card needs alternation** (the card's whole `grep`/`sed` surface was swept for it), and no pattern sits inside `grep -E`, `grep -P`, `sed -E` or `awk` with an escaped pipe, and no bare `\|` appears in a `grep` without `-E`, where it would be a literal. **A future repair here prefers no-alternation over correct-escaping.** (The row's own shell pipes are GFM table escapes and **must** be: a pipe cannot appear unescaped in a table cell. That is unavoidable and harmless in kind, because a pipe copied without de-escaping breaks every pipe in the row loudly and immediately, where the regex case failed silently. The rendered form — which is what the reader sees and what the row means — parses, and so does the raw form for every row except V0, which was already like that and is untouched.) **(e) stopping the server after a settled `ready` paints nothing — primary, positive, and the assertion part (ii) exists to satisfy.** After the settled `ready`, the marker request and its 3 s wait, the row signals the server pid from `main.rs:221` (`SIGTERM`, escalating to `SIGKILL` on that same pid; never `pkill`, never a pattern — C-ISO@1 rule 7) and then requires, 3 s later, that the **whole-display snapshot is byte-identical to the previous one**, that the **identified app-owned set is byte-identical**, and that **the identified main window's id is still present**. It **fails** if the shell painted an error screen — a new owned window — or if it took the app window down with it, and it is the witness an implementation carrying only part (i) fails: it turns on the **presence** of a window the guard must not create and on the continued **presence** of the one it must not destroy, neither of which the old title-grep could see. **(f) anything arriving after a settled `ready` is logged and ignored — the log half supporting the same positive window assertion.** The same post-`ready` kill produces the `ChildGone` the reader thread sends the moment `child.wait()` returns (`main.rs:250-251`): the row requires its log line `apunta: the server exited before it was ready (…)` (`main.rs:331`) to be **present** — logged, not swallowed — and no `apunta: the error window could not be opened`, **while (e)'s window-identity assertions carry the "paints nothing" half**. The wording is the whole clause, "any line after a settled `ready`", which also covers the `fatal` arm at `:307-317` whose unconditional `show_error` at `:313` becomes reachable with `:298` gone; **no current code path produces a `fatal` after a settled `ready`** (`server/src/index.ts` writes `Fatal` only at startup), so the row asserts the clause over the events the run can produce and **must not manufacture one** — a server-side producer would be Stop condition 2. **(d1), (d2), (e) and (f) together are what "the child stays distinguishable from the reader thread at shutdown" means** (Fixed decision 6); if the change cannot satisfy them, that is Stop condition 3. The row runs four launches, signals **every** pid it started by pid and never by pattern, releases the port holder it started before the launch that needs the port free, and leaves 7860 free with 7717 never contacted. **The port holder is released by a `trap`, not only by the explicit `kill` on the happy path.** A `SIGINT`, a closed terminal or a harness timeout used to leave the `python3` listener on 7860 for the rest of its life, and the **next** `sandbox.mjs env --port 7860` then refuses the port — which on this card's last attempt costs a run for a reason the row itself created. So the row sets `trap "kill $HP 2>/dev/null" EXIT INT TERM` immediately after `HP=$!`, and the `EXIT` arm is the load-bearing one: it fires on **every** way the row's shell ends, including the `exit 3` and `exit 1` sites and a `SIGTERM`. (The **double quotes are required, not a style choice**: the whole body runs inside `bash -c '…'`, so it must contain **zero single quotes** — the trap's pid expands when the signal arrives, which is what is wanted.) **Two honest limits, measured rather than assumed.** A `SIGINT` delivered to the row's shell **does not fire an `INT` trap in a non-interactive `bash`** — the shell ignores `SIGINT` and keeps running, so there is no leak at that moment (it is still holding the port it needs); the `EXIT`/`TERM` arms then release the holder on the `SIGTERM` that follows, which is what a harness timeout sends. And a holder signalled **directly** with `SIGINT` ignores it, because a non-interactive shell sets `SIGINT` to `SIG_IGN` in the background jobs it starts. **`SIGKILL` to the row's shell cannot be trapped by anything**, which is why the holder's own life is bounded well inside the row's worst case: `time.sleep(300)`, against a remaining path of at most 60 s + 5 s + 60 s + 20 s + 5 s ≈ 150 s after the holder exists. A row that fails (a), (b), (c) or (f) is a genuine lifecycle regression **even when V3 passed**, and it may not be relaxed, re-scoped or reported as a known issue |

## Stop conditions

1. **A change that would re-navigate after `ready`.** Anything that can call
   `show_main`, `close_window` or `show_error` a second time on a path reachable
   after the first `ready` — re-navigating on every forwarded line, re-showing
   the main window per line, treating a later `Ready` as a fresh launch. C-BRIDGE@1
   rule 1 makes the single navigation load-bearing, and V4(a)/(b) are the
   assertions. Stop and report; do not "make it idempotent".
2. **The fix needs anything outside `drive`.** In particular: a capability or a
   `tauri.conf.json` edit; a `server/` change to make a line appear (a new log
   line, a new route, a new env var, a build flag); a new harness or test file;
   a change to the reader thread at `:236-252`; or a re-bundle.
   **If the loop turns out to need more than the forwarding loop, that is a
   finding to report, not a scope to widen into** — the card says "report rather
   than widen" precisely because the obvious-looking widening is the one that
   reintroduces an IPC surface or a second navigation.
3. **The child cannot be distinguished from the reader thread at shutdown, or
   the post-`ready` guard cannot be expressed inside the two parts Fixed decision
   1 names.** Once the loop keeps forwarding, `ChildGone` — and any other line,
   including `fatal` — arrives on the same channel after `ready` as well as before
   it. If the change cannot both keep painting an error screen on a
   **pre-`ready`** exit and keep **not** painting one on a **post-`ready`** exit,
   the shell has lost the distinction that C-BRIDGE@1 rule 7's early exit depends
   on. **A third part to the change is also this stop:** Fixed decision 1
   authorises exactly two parts, in the same file and the same function — (i) and
   (ii). A new arm, a second or recomputed `settled` flag, a moved assignment, a
   rewritten `show_error`, an edit to the `fatal` arm or an edit to the terminal
   drain is not a third part — it is a scope widening, and it belongs to the
   coordinator on AM-138/AM-140, not to this attempt. Stop and report; do not
   resolve it by re-navigating, by suppressing the error screen, or by weakening
   V4(e) or V4(f).
4. **`Ready` cannot be kept on stderr while forwarding continues**, or the
   ordering between the `ready` line and a later line cannot be observed.
   P3.4's harness reads both, and a channel that reports the second without the
   first cannot be read at all.
5. **V1 is red in `main.rs`, in any of the thirteen tests.** Report and stop. A
   navigation guard, a nonce check or an unknown-type arm that has to be
   weakened for this change to compile is a stop (Fixed decision 8).
6. **`build/linux-resources/` is absent**, so V0 and the launching rows cannot
   run. Record `NOT RUN` naming it and let the coordinator run P3.1's V1. Do
   not run `scripts/v2/package-linux-resources.sh` from this card: it is L3 work
   and it re-fetches A06 (HS-3).
7. **V2's file list names a second path**, or a lint/typecheck failure lands in
   a file outside May edit — including `cargo fmt --check` naming
   `src-tauri/src/bridge.rs`. Report it; do not reformat, do not fix, and do not
   stage anything. AM-136 records what a single careless `git add` already cost
   this plan.
8. **The app cannot be observed from outside** — no display, no `xvfb-run`, no
   window title or geometry readable, no window belonging to the launch's own pid
   found at all, or a window the row cannot **name** (V4 needs exactly one window
   titled `Apunta`, owned by that pid, at or above the app's own 880×600 minimum).
   Then V3 and V4 are `NOT RUN` with that cause and the card **does not** fall
   back to asserting the behaviour from the source text. A reading of the diff is
   not a run, and an unidentifiable window list is not a pass: a row that
   reported "no second window appeared" or "no error window appeared" about
   windows it could not name would satisfy (b), (e) and (f) **vacuously** — which
   is precisely how attempt 2's V4 went `NOT RUN` while the log halves read
   correct, and precisely the false green this card will not ship. Both rows run
   the launch and every probe inside one `xvfb-run -a bash -c` precisely so that
   this condition means "no display here" rather than "the probe read the wrong
   one", and V4 pins the screen size so that a clamped window is not mistaken for
   the app's. **No window manager is installed on this host and acquiring one is
   outside the card**, so this condition is a `NOT RUN` to be reported, never a
   reason to fall back to a weaker witness: if the windows cannot be identified
   by owner pid and exact title on a bare `xvfb-run`, say so and stop.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-BRIDGE@1 Shell and server

**Built by** P3.3 (lifecycle) and P3.4 (security). **Proven by** P3.6 and
P5.5. **Consumers:** Tauri shell, server, web update notice.

1. The shell spawns the server itself and trusts only its own child's
   stdout. The server prints exactly one JSON line when listening:
   `{"type":"ready","port":7717,"nonce":"<from env>","version":"x.y.z","protocol":1}`.
   The shell navigates only after reading this line with its own nonce. No
   health-poll trust.
2. Further messages are JSON lines. Server to shell: `ready`, `fatal{code}`,
   `update_request{action:"check"|"download"|"install"}`,
   `quiesce_result{ok, blockers[]}`. Shell to server (stdin):
   `update_status{state, version?, code?}`, `quiesce{}`, `shutdown{}`.
   Unknown message types are logged and ignored.
3. The web page talks only to the server over HTTP. Update endpoints
   (`GET /api/app/update`, `POST /api/app/update/{check,download,install}`)
   exist only when the server was started by the shell; in browser mode
   they return 404.
4. **No Tauri IPC from web content.** No capabilities for any webview
   origin, `withGlobalTauri: false`, no custom `invoke_handler` commands.
5. Navigation: the main window may load only `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/…`.
   Any other navigation or new window is cancelled. `https:` links the app
   intends to open (none required in v2) would open in the system browser
   only if listed in the shell's allowlist; the list is empty in v2.
6. The server sends a Content-Security-Policy on every HTML response,
   including the boot-error page, with at least: `default-src 'self'`,
   `script-src 'self'`, `connect-src 'self'`, `object-src 'none'`,
   `base-uri 'none'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`. Any extra source must be
   justified in the card's evidence by a failing test without it.
7. If the server writes `fatal` or exits before `ready`, the shell shows a
   bilingual error screen with the message code (not a spinner).

**Rejection examples.** A dummy process on the port answering `/api/health`
→ never navigated to (the shell never polls it). A page that injects
`<script>` via imported Markdown → blocked by CSP and cannot reach Tauri.

## C-ISO@1 Isolation and the sandbox wrapper

**Built by** P0.3. **Proven by** P0.3 (negative tests) and Q1.1.
**Consumers:** every card that starts a server, opens a real database, runs
e2e, runs `check:format`/`check:refine`, runs a real-model eval or launches
the app.

**Interface** (`scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs`, Node, no dependencies):

| Command | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs run --port <p> -- <cmd...>` | Creates run folder, starts server, verifies ownership, runs `<cmd>` with the sandbox environment, stops only what it started, exits with `<cmd>`'s code |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port <p>` | Creates run folder only, prints `export` lines for tools that start their own server (Playwright) |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs selftest` | Runs the negative cases below; exit 0 only if all refuse correctly |

**Rules**
1. Run folder: `/tmp/apunta-v2/<runId>/` with `data/`, `logs/`, `tmp/`,
   mode `700`. `runId` = UTC timestamp + 8 random hex characters.
   `realpath` of every path must stay under `/tmp/apunta-v2/`; a symlink that
   escapes is refused.
2. Port must be an integer 7800 to 7889 and free (checked by binding, then
   released immediately before the server binds). 7717 is always refused.
   7890 to 7899 are reserved for the updater test server (C-UPD) and refused
   here.
3. The data folder is never the platform default. The wrapper computes the
   default with `platformDataDir()` (C-PATH) **as a string only** and refuses
   if the sandbox path equals it or is inside it. It never lists or opens the
   default.
4. Server environment: `APUNTA_DATA_DIR`, `APUNTA_PORT`, `APUNTA_NO_OPEN=1`,
   `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID=<runId>`, `APUNTA_V2=1`. When `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID` is
   set, `/api/health` includes `"testRunId"`; the field never appears
   otherwise.
5. Ownership check: the wrapper polls `/api/health` for up to 30 s and
   proceeds only if `testRunId` equals its `runId`. Anything else (no
   answer, a different id, no id) is refused and the child is stopped.
6. Child command environment adds `APUNTA_CHECK_URL`, `APUNTA_E2E_PORT`,
   `APUNTA_V2=1`.
7. Cleanup kills only the process group the wrapper created. Never `pkill`,
   never the Ollama daemon.
8. When `APUNTA_V2=1`: Playwright sets `reuseExistingServer: false`;
   `scripts/check-note-format.mjs` and `scripts/check-refine.mjs` exit 2 if
   `APUNTA_CHECK_URL` is unset or points at port 7717.

**Normal example.** `sandbox.mjs run --port 7801 -- npm run check:format`
→ run folder created, server answers with the matching `testRunId`, the
check runs against `http://127.0.0.1:7801`, server stopped, exit code of the
check.

**Rejection examples** (each must be a `selftest` case, refused before any
database is opened): `--port 7717`; `--port 7890`; port in use by a dummy
listener; a dummy server on the port answering `/api/health` with 200 but no
or wrong `testRunId`; run folder symlinked outside `/tmp/apunta-v2/`;
`APUNTA_DATA_DIR` equal to the platform default string.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

**Redirect admission (rule 1).** A redirect is followed only when its `Location`
resolves to `https:`, port 443, no user-info, no fragment, a host the row's
*Redirect hosts* cell admits, and a query whose every parameter name appears in
that row's *Allowed query keys* cell. A parameter name outside the cell is
refused (`query_key_not_allowed`) before the URL is requested. `none` means the
row admits no query at all, so any query is `query_not_allowed` — that is the
default and it is unchanged. No row admits a query by wildcard, a prefix or a
blanket permission, and the cell is the complete list: adding a name is a
plan-editor amendment (AM-042).

**Why A07's names are safe to enumerate.** The ten names are the AWS
CloudFront signed-URL parameter set plus Hugging Face's Xet and
`response-content-*` parameters, observed on 2026-09-26 across all six C-STT
artifacts and the one speech artifact, each answering `302` to
`us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`). They cannot change
*which* bytes arrive: the path is fixed by the pinned catalogue URL and the
bytes are verified against the pinned `sha256`, and the committed name is the
entry's own `sizeBytes` path, so the two `response-content-*` parameters can
only shape headers a client would have sent anyway. The card's own worry — "a
query string is where a download URL turns into a message" — is about
*outbound* data, and none of these names carries any: the probe records the
**names** only and writes every value as `<redacted>`, so a signature is never
in the repository, the evidence or any log.

**The four-arm comparison (A13, A14, A15).** Added 2026-09-26 on the owner's
approval, for one measurement round and nothing else. The arms are
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` as the control (A08; already present, and A08's "never pulled
if present" still holds), plus A13, A14 and A15. Three rules bind the round and
are not negotiable per run:

1. **No candidate becomes a default.** A07's "selected one only" and A08's tag
   are unchanged. The round measures; it does not promote.
2. **The licence of A14 and A15 is unknown to the coordinator and must be found
   before either is pulled.** These are models downloaded by the user at setup,
   so L-POLICY@1's row for that applies: per the publisher's licence, shown and
   recorded. Prism's licence for these repositories is not asserted here because
   it was not verified — anyone pulling them records the licence text and the
   URL it came from, or reports `BLOCKED`. Guessing it is exactly the failure
   this manifest exists to prevent.
3. **The GPU is not shared.** One model loaded at a time, `keep_alive` set so
   each unloads after its arm, and no arm runs while the owner is testing on the
   machine or a live instance is in use. A four-arm run is long and real.

**Fraunces (A16) follows Kalam, not a build-time download.** Both source TTFs live in `docs/v2/assets/` with their OFL texts, and `build-brand-fraunces.py` reads the local file and touches no network — regenerating the wordmark in six years must not depend on a `/tmp` file or a download working. A16 permits exactly that one fetch, to obtain the file committed beside it. Fraunces is a **variable** font; the committed cut is the variable one, and the generator pins `wght 500`, `opsz 14`, `SOFT 0`, `WONK 0`, because a static instance could not set optical size and an unpinned variable font would not reproduce. The TTF is never bundled: the app ships outlines only.

**Owner-run items.** `apt` needs `sudo`. The coordinator writes the exact
command to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, stops the dependent cards, and
waits; the owner runs it. Agents never enter a password.

**Ollama.** Before any pull, run `ollama list`; if the tag exists, do not pull.
Record the digest with `ollama show <tag>`. Real-model runs set Ollama's
`keep_alive` so evaluation models unload after use, and run only one model
at a time, to avoid starving the live instance.

## 2. Development tools already present

Anything already installed on the PC (git, Python, Piper if present,
whisper-cli, Ollama) may be used as found. Record its version in evidence.

## 3. L-POLICY@1 Licences

One rule, applied per object reviewed (a tool, a library, a model file, a
voice, a dictionary, generated audio are separate objects).

| Object | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Code or data **shipped** in the app or installer | MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Unicode, OFL-1.1 (fonts), CC0, CC-BY-4.0 (data, with attribution) |
| The one pre-approved exception | Spanish dictionary **data** under an MPL option of a multi-licence, shipped unmodified in its own files, election and obligations stated in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and `docs/decisions.md` |
| Development-only tools never shipped or linked | any OSI licence, including GPL (Piper) |
| Generated fixtures committed to the repo | only if the voice's model card permits redistribution of generated audio; otherwise generate at test time into the sandbox and never commit |
| Models downloaded by the user at setup | per the publisher's licence, shown in setup, recorded in the catalogue |
| System libraries bundled into an AppImage (for example WebKitGTK, LGPL) | allowed for **test builds**; **public distribution requires owner review** (listed in the final report) |

Anything else: do not add it; the card reports `BLOCKED` with the licence
text found. A dependency's MIT wrapper does not change its data's licence.
